# Appeal of Denial — Total Hip Replacement (CPT 27130)

**RE:** Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
**Member:** Rowan Brooks
**Member ID:** W772624569
**Reference Number:** POC-A5F6D22435-38075
**Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-08-07
**Plan:** Security Health Plan (Commercial/ACA), Wisconsin

Dear Security Health Plan Appeals Department,

I am writing to appeal the denial of my total hip replacement surgery (CPT 27130), as stated in the notice dated 2026-08-07, reference number POC-A5F6D22435-38075. My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking the plan to reconsider its decision.

## The Governing Policy

The denial notice states that the review was made "under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria," and lists the reason as: the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. The policy materials I have been given for this review are from the **eviCore CMM-311/312/313/314/315/601/606/609 series** (generic EviCore editions), available at: https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2025-08/EviCore_CMM-311%20Knee%20Replacement%20Arthroplasty_V2.0.2025_Eff11.05.2025_upd08.12.2025.pdf

I want to note something important: the specific criteria language provided to me is titled "Knee Replacement/Arthroplasty" and addresses knee, not hip, surgery. My procedure is a **total hip replacement**, not a knee procedure. Because I have not been given the plan's specific hip replacement medical necessity criteria, I am not able to confirm that the correct criteria were applied to my case, and I do not think it would be fair to either of us for me to argue against criteria that may not even be the ones used to deny my surgery.

One provision in the materials I do have is written broadly enough to apply to my situation, since it addresses lower extremity joint pain generally rather than the knee specifically:

> "Non-Surgical Management (with regard to the treatment of lower extremity joint pain) any provider-directed non-surgical treatment, which has been demonstrated in the scientific literature as efficacious and/or is considered reasonable care in the treatment of lower extremity joint pain."

My medical records show that I completed exactly this kind of provider-directed, evidence-based conservative treatment before surgery was recommended:

- 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait (2026-02-22 to 2026-06-14, 16 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note)
- 6 months of NSAID therapy with inadequate relief
- A corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-29, which gave only 3 weeks of partial relief
- 24 months of progressive hip pain unrelieved by rest
- A weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph on 2026-06-09 showing joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes
- Functional limitations including cane-assisted ambulation limited to one block and inability to put on shoes unassisted
- A physical exam with positive provocative testing and pain-limited range of motion on the affected side

This record shows that I did not go straight to surgery — I completed a substantial course of non-surgical management first, and it did not resolve my pain or restore my function. My surgeon has reviewed this history and has documented that surgery is medically necessary.

## Request for the Applicable Criteria in Writing

Because the guideline excerpts provided to me address knee replacement rather than hip replacement, I am formally requesting that Security Health Plan provide me, in writing, the specific medical necessity criteria it actually applied when reviewing my hip replacement request. I understand Security Health Plan maintains its own "Total Hip Replacement Surgery" policy on its PolicyTech site, and I am requesting a copy of that policy. I am also requesting copies of the plan's "Back Surgical Procedures" policy and any hip impingement–related policy, as I understand these currently redirect to a Sanford Health login page that I am unable to access as a plan member. I am entitled to know the exact criteria used to deny my claim, and I would like the opportunity to respond to the correct standard.

## What I Am Asking For

I am asking Security Health Plan to reconsider the denial of my total hip replacement (CPT 27130) in light of the records above, and to provide the specific hip replacement medical necessity criteria that were applied to my case, along with the other policies requested above. I understand my appeal must be received by **2027-02-03** (180 days from the date of the denial notice). I will send this appeal to the address printed on my denial letter, or, if that is not available, I will call the number on the back of my insurance card to confirm where member appeals should be filed.

Thank you for your time and attention to my case.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Rowan Brooks
